Mali.title: Strengthening the operational capabilities of the FAMa: The Transitional President presents new aircraft to the Air Force
Mali.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2020, at Modibo Keïta-Sénou International Airport, the Transitional President, Head of State and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi Goïta, officially handed over the keys to an Ilyushin IL-76 strategic transport aircraft and Mi-24 and Mi-8 helicopters to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa). . This acquisition strengthens the operational and logistical capabilities of the national defence force.

Mali.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: The army strikes terrorist positions in Abeïbara and Sévaré
Mali.summary: According to the press release, the first assembly point, located between 8 and 10 kilometres north and north-east of Abeïbara, housed several individuals as well as military equipment, including vehicles, and a fuel depot. The second, located 33 kilometres south-west of Sévaré, also housed several individuals and military equipment, including motorcycles. .

Mali.title: Mali: The army receives a new batch of aircraft
Mali.summary: Mali: The army takes delivery of a new batch of aircraft The Malian army is expanding its air fleet. On Monday, 16 November 2026, it took delivery of a new batch of aircraft on the tarmac of the presidential pavilion at Modibo Keita International Airport in Bamako. The Transitional President, Army General Assimi Goïta, presided over the ceremony in the presence of civil and military authorities.

Mali.title: Bamako: The body of a man pulled from the Niger River
Mali.summary: A body was removed from the Niger River on Sunday evening, in Badalabougou, near the Martyrs' Bridge. It was fishermen who spotted it and raised the alarm. The victim is a man of about 30 years old.

Mali.title: STRENGTHENING OPERATIONAL CAPABILITIES: The Transitional President presents a new batch of aircraft to the Malian Armed Forces
Mali.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2026, the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi Goïta, presided over the official ceremony at the Presidential Pavilion of Modibo Keïta-Sénou International Airport for the handover of new aircraft to the Malian Armed Forces. This allocation reflects the desire of the highest authorities to continue efforts to modernise the defence force.

Mali.title: National Defence: The Air Force is strengthening its fleet with an IL-76 strategic aircraft and Mi-24 and Mi-8 helicopters
Mali.summary: STRENGTHENING THE OPERATIONAL CAPABILITIES OF THE FAMa: The Transitional President hands over new aircraft to the Air Force The Transitional President, Head of State and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi Goïta, officially handed over the keys to an Ilyushin IL-76 strategic transport aircraft and Mi-24 and Mi-17 helicopters at Président Modibo Keïta-Sénou International Airport on Monday, 16 November 2026.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Mali: The National Defence Forces Equipped with New Aircraft
Mali.summary: Bamako, 16 November (AMAP) The official ceremony for the handover of new aircraft was presided over on Monday at Modibo Keïta – Sénou International Airport by the Transitional President, Army General Assimi Goïta, in the presence of civil and military authorities, AMAP reported. . This new batch of aircraft includes an Ilyushin Il-76 strategic transport aircraft, four Mi-8 utility helicopters and two Mi-24 attack helicopters.

Mali.title: Mali: Assimi Goïta equips the army with 7 new military aircraft, including 4 Mi-24 helicopters
Mali.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2026, the President of Mali's Transitional Government, Army General Assimi Goïta, presided over a ceremony at Bamako's Président Modibo Keïta International Airport to hand over new aircraft to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa). This delivery covers seven aircraft. These include four Mi-24 attack helicopters, two Mi-8 utility helicopters and one Ilyushin Il-76 strategic transport aircraft.

Mali.title: Defence: Mali strengthens its air fleet with seven new aircraft
Mali.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2026, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) took delivery of seven new aircraft to enhance their operational capabilities. Funded entirely from the national budget as part of cooperation with Russia, this equipment includes a strategic transport aircraft, four utility helicopters and two attack helicopters. .

Mali.title: GMS roundabout–Samé–Kati section: The...
Mali.summary: GMS roundabout–Samé–Kati section: The demolition of buildings and installations within the project's right-of-way begins this Monday, 16 November 2026. The demolition of buildings and installations located within the right-of-way of the GMS Roundabout–Samé–Kati section will begin this Monday The announcement was made by the Ministers of Transport and Infrastructure, Urban Planning, Housing, State Property, Regional Planning and Population in a joint statement released on Sunday evening.

Mali.title: The Malian Air Force receives new helicopters and a transport aircraft
Mali.summary: The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) are strengthening their air fleet. On Monday, 16 November, the Transitional President and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi Goïta, presided over the handover ceremony for new aircraft at Modibo Keïta International Airport in Bamako, in the presence of the military hierarchy. .

Mali.title: GMS roundabout–Samé–Kati section: The demolition of buildings and installations within the project's right-of-way will begin on Monday, 16 November 2026.
Mali.summary: The announcement was made by the Ministers of Transport and Infrastructure, Urban Planning, Housing, State Property, Regional Planning and Population in a joint statement released on Sunday evening. According to the press release, this operation is part of the clearing of the rights of way essential for carrying out the dual carriageway development works on this important section of road.

Mali.title: Guinea deports 1,557 West African nationals after they were convicted of illegal gold mining
Mali.summary: The Guinean authorities deported 1,557 citizens from West African countries, mostly from Mali and Burkina Faso, to their countries of origin, after they were convicted of illegal gold mining, according to Radio France Internationale. The radio station reported that the deportation operation took place on Saturday, 14 November, involving 44 vehicles and helicopters, and under tight security.

Mali.title: Guinea-Mali border: 1,557 gold miners of various nationalities tried, pardoned and deported to Kourémalé
Mali.summary: Guinea-Mali border: 1,557 gold panners of various nationalities tried, pardoned and deported to Kourémalé On Friday, 13 November 2026, the Guinean authorities released 1,557 people of various nationalities who had been arrested at mining sites for illegal gold panning activities. . According to our information, all these individuals were tried by various Guinean courts before being pardoned by the Head of State and deported to the Malian border.

Mali.title: Guinea: Is JNIM threatening the country from Mali? What a field study reveals
Mali.summary: On 25 October 2026, the Konrad Adenauer Foundation published a study on the establishment of JNIM, a group linked to al-Qaeda, in south-western Mali, on the border with Guinea. Conducted by the SITOC organisation in June and July 2026, the survey is based on 68 testimonies collected in south-western Mali and Upper Guinea. Local officials, representatives of civil society, security stakeholders, gold miners and transhumant herders were interviewed.

Mali.title: Kourémalé: 1,557 gold miners of various nationalities pardoned and escorted to the Guinea-Mali border
Mali.summary: A total of 1,557 gold miners of various nationalities, who were arrested at mining sites for "illegal gold mining activities", were tried and sentenced in Conakry. They were granted a pardon on Friday, 13 November 2020, and then taken to Kourémalé, on the border between Guinea and Mali, on Saturday, 14 November, by the Guinean authorities, with a view to returning them to their respective countries.

Mali.title: Mali: Mauritania, the Maghreb country most exposed to the crisis, according to the IEEE
Mali.summary: On 13 November 2023, the Spanish Institute for Strategic Studies (IEEE) published an analysis identifying Mauritania as the Maghreb country most directly threatened by the deteriorating situation in Mali. Authored by analyst Jaime Bello, the text specifies that his views do not represent the position of the Spanish Ministry of Defence. According to him, Nouakchott is under three pressures at once: a porous border, the terrorist threat and the mass influx of refugees.

Mali.title: Kayes: A 45-year-old suspect arrested for sexually abusing an 8-year-old girl
Mali.summary: As part of Operation 'KOKADJÈ', initiated by the Regional Director of the National Police of Kayes, Chief Superintendent Tapa Oury Diallo, the Police Station of the 1st Arrondissement of Kayes, headed by Chief Superintendent Daouda Cissé, arrested an individual suspected of sexually abusing an eight-year-old girl on 7 November 2024. . Alerted by a complaint from the victim's family, the police immediately began investigations that led to the arrest of the suspect, identified by the initials M.T., aged 45 and residing in the Lafiabougou-Faradabougouni district in Kayes.

Mali.title: Illegal gold mining: Is what is prohibited in Guinea permitted in Mali?
Mali.summary: Illegal gold panning: Is what is prohibited in Guinea permitted in Mali? Since the beginning of this month, Mali has been facing an influx into its territory of several nationals from the subregion, particularly from Burkina Faso. They are being turned away from Guinea-Conakry due to illegal gold panning.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: 100 new stars to illuminate Avenue Kwame-Nkrumah
Burkina Faso.summary: One hundred Burkinabé and foreign personalities now have their stars on Avenue Kwame-Nkrumah, in the heart of Ouagadougou. Their names are engraved on stelae installed as part of the second edition of the "Street of Stars", an initiative of the Sotigui Academy. .

Burkina Faso.title: Defence: The FAMa are strengthening their fleet with new aircraft acquired using their own funds
Burkina Faso.summary: The official handover ceremony was presided over by the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi Goïta, in the presence of civil and military authorities. Fully funded from the national budget and acquired as part of cooperation with the Russian Federation, these aircraft are intended to increase the army's strategic mobility and logistical autonomy.

Burkina Faso.title: AES: Ministers prepare for the upcoming summit in Ouagadougou
Burkina Faso.summary: The three countries reviewed the implementation of the Year II roadmap. Operational decisions are expected at the next College of Heads of State. The Extraordinary Council of Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States met on 11 and 12 November in Ouagadougou.

Burkina Faso.title: The legal front
Burkina Faso.summary: On Friday, 13 November 2020, the Public Prosecutor at the Ouagadougou Court of Appeal held a press briefing on the legal proceedings brought against 45 individuals and legal entities for various offences related to terrorism and breaches of public order. . This statement by the judicial authorities serves as a reminder that, in a state facing a war that threatens its very existence, the defence of the nation is not limited to fighting terrorists.

Burkina Faso.title: Legal proceedings: landmark cases revealed
Burkina Faso.summary: On Friday, 13 November 2020, Pinguedewindé Désiré Sawadogo, the Public Prosecutor at the Ouagadougou Court of Appeal, held a press conference in Ouagadougou on the status of certain cases currently under investigation at the Specialised Judicial Division for the Suppression of Acts of Terrorism of the Ouaga II High Court. . Since 30 September 2022, under the leadership of the President of Burkina Faso, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, Burkina Faso has been waging a successful and fearless fight against terrorism.

Niger.title: African Road Safety Day: Niger focuses on discipline and strengthening checks to reduce road accidents
Niger.summary: Le Niger a célébré, le dimanche 15 novembre 2026, la 15è édition de la Journée africaine de la sécurité routière sous le thème : « Zéro tolérance sur nos routes : sensibiliser, contrôler, inspecter et réprimer ». Instituée par l’Union africaine, cette journée est observée chaque troisième dimanche du mois de novembre. Elle est couplée à la Journée mondiale du souvenir des victimes des accidents de la route, une journée officielle des Nations Unies.

Niger.title: NATIONAL POLICE: GENERAL ABOUBACAR OUMAROU, A SEASONED OFFICER AT THE HELM
Niger.summary: From the fight against illicit drug trafficking to command responsibilities within the National Police, Police Commissioner General Aboubacar Issaka Oumarou is taking the helm of the DGPN. His career has been marked by professional experience in Niger and in several international United Nations missions. The General Directorate of the National Police (DGPN) has a new head .

Niger.title: 15th edition of the JASR: 7,116 accidents resulted in 1,245 deaths and 4,439 serious injuries in Niger in 2023
Niger.summary: Niamey, 15 November (ANP) – In a message delivered on Saturday, 14 November, the day before the celebration of the 15th edition of African Road Safety Day, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, Colonel Major Abdourahamane Amadou, announced that, in 2025, Niger had recorded 7,116 road accidents, which resulted in 1,245 deaths and 4,439 serious injuries in the country.
